stories.headline: Anthropic is spending $100M to train 10,000 engineers on Claude
stories.blurb: The company behind Claude is launching a free training program to teach enterprise engineers how to build with its AI models. The goal: train 10,000 people and close what Anthropic calls the 'enterprise AI talent gap' — companies want to deploy AI but lack in-house expertise.
stories.why_it_matters: AI companies are now competing on education, not just model performance
stories.original_headline: Anthropic invests $100 million to train 10,000 engineers and tackle the enterprise AI talent gap

stories.headline: OpenAI's Dot agents can order your dinner between spreadsheet tasks
stories.blurb: OpenAI's new Dots platform gives you AI agents that handle work tasks but can also grab you a burrito. Unlike Meta's friendlier Muse, Dots feels like enterprise software first—workplace tools that happen to run errands on the side.
stories.why_it_matters: AI agents are landing in your work apps, not just as chatbots but as coworkers who multitask.
stories.original_headline: OpenAI’s Dot agent is enterprise software that can also order your dinner

stories.headline: Apple is locking down Mac disk access because of AI agents
stories.blurb: Apple is adding new permission controls for full disk access on Mac, citing the security risk from AI agents that can read and modify files autonomously. The changes mean users will need to explicitly grant apps deeper system access, even if they've already approved it once.
stories.why_it_matters: First major OS vendor treating AI agents as a distinct security threat class.
stories.original_headline: Apple will limit Mac disk access as AI agents ‘substantially’ increase risk

stories.headline: Google's AI model topped CDC's flu hospitalization forecasts
stories.blurb: The Centers for Disease Control ranked Google's science AI model first among all submissions for predicting flu-related hospital admissions. Google applied its medical AI work to public health forecasting, outperforming traditional epidemiological models in accuracy.
stories.why_it_matters: AI can now predict hospital strain weeks ahead, giving health systems time to staff up.
stories.original_headline: Google's AI ranks #1 for predicting flu hospitalizations.
